title: Iran War Set To EXPLODE Before Midterms
summary: Commentators argue a US-Iran deal is now unlikely because Iran no longer trusts Trump to keep one, and that the US and Israel will soon restart the war with Iran on a larger scale.

assertions.quote: Israel, uh and America, are going to restart uh the war with Iran on a much, much larger scale.

verdicts.note: At the time of the video a third US carrier was reported heading to the region, but whether a new round begins cannot yet be judged.

Polymarket's price that the US-Iran ceasefire holds falls from 83.5% through October 31 to 36% through November 30 and 29% through December 31, 2026, implying about a 70% chance of a new US strike on Iran before the year ends.
As of April 2026 the paper says it is uncertain whether Trump would return to military action if talks collapsed, and leaves a resumption open.

assertions.quote: he doesn't have the maturity needed to be able to go through a negotiation and get a deal.

verdicts.note: Both rounds of US-Iran talks since 2025 ended with US or Israeli attacks, and Iran then refused talks without guarantees against renewed war; one case consistent with the claim.

assertions.quote: the likelihood of a deal is now increasingly diminished and likelihood of a major escalation is growing.

verdicts.note: A forecast about ongoing talks whose outcome is not yet known.
As of April 2026, the US and Israeli demands (giving up 60% enriched material, ending enrichment, abandoning missiles) are seen by Iran as unrealistic, leaving a resumption of war possible.

assertions.quote: The Iranians will not be able to get back to 60% enriched uranium, for instance, if they allow if they agree to ship it out.

verdicts.note: Iran's negotiating intentions are not on the public record.
Iran demanded full lifting of sanctions, guarantees against future war and its right to enrich, and rejects handing over its 60% enriched material as unrealistic.

assertions.quote: I don't think Trump is in charge at all.

verdicts.note: Trump set and extended the deadlines and accepted a ceasefire to which Israel was not a party, while Israel claimed it would comply with whatever Washington asked.
